item.title: Manhunt after car carrying explosives crashes in police chase
item.description:
Manhunt after car carrying explosives crashes in police chase

July 29, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Police are trying to trace the occupants of a car that crashed at high speed in Amsterdam while carrying high explosives, causing dozens of homes to be evacuated.

The black BMW M1 was being pursued by Dutch police after their German colleagues spotted it at the scene of a cashpoint explosion in Fürth, Hessen, around 250km from the Dutch border.

Witnesses described how it was driven into Nierkerkestraat, Osdorp, at high speed, hit a speed bump and crashed. The occupants, at least one of whom was armed, got out and fled on foot.

A specialist explosives team quickly arrived on the scene and cleared all houses within a 100m radius after discovering bomb-making materials in the vehicle.

Residents had to stay out of their homes for nearly nine hours following the incident, which happened at around 1pm on Tuesday, until the car was taken away on a tow truck.

Police appealed for witnesses to come forward, as well as anyone with information about the storage of explosives in the area. It is not clear how many people were in the car.

Cross-border gangs

German police said no money was stolen in the attack on the cash machine, but the building where it was located was badly damaged by the blast.

The Osdorp area of Amsterdam is known to be a base for gangs that carry out cross-border raids on German cashpoints, which tend to contain more money than those in the Netherlands because cash is still widely used there.

Last month seven people were injured and an entire block of flats had to be evacuated after an explosion in a basement gym next to the Osdorper Ban which was caused by home-made explosives.

Police arrested two men aged 24 and 23, both of whom were among the casualties. Prosecutors said they were suspected of planning explosions and possessing explosive materials.

item.title: Three arrested in dawn raids in anti-terrorism probe
item.description:
Three arrested in dawn raids in anti-terrorism probe

July 29, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Police have arrested three teenagers in overnight raids in Eindhoven, Rotterdam and Alkmaar as part of a a counter-terrorism investigation.

The three suspects, aged between 16 and 19, were arrested at their homes in the early hours of Wednesday.

Video footage from Rotterdam showed around half a dozen police wearing riot helmets and body armour going into a house and leading a blindfolded man to a car.

The Eindhovens Dagblad newspaper said the 19-year-old man was arrested in Jan van Eyckgracht, a street in the Burghplan neighbourhood.

Three years ago he was reportedly arrested at the same address on suspicion of planning attacks on nightclubs and police stations in Belgium via social media channels. No attacks actually took place.

He was given a 112-day jail sentence, a 200-hour community service order and banned from travelling out of the Netherlands after the court heard he had talked about joining the terrorist organisation Islamic State in Afghanistan.

No further details were available of the arrest in Alkmaar, Noord-Holland.

item.title: Fire destroys youth care facility in Beekbergen
item.description:
Fire destroys youth care facility in Beekbergen

July 29, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Firefighters in the Gelderland town of Beekbergen are still trying to contain a blaze on Wednesday that destroyed a youth care facility.

The local safety board says teams are “extinguishing hidden pockets of fire” from the inferno that broke out late Tuesday evening.

Around 20 people were evacuated and one person was rushed to the hospital. The cause of the fire is not yet clear.

The flames quickly spread to a nearby wooded area and more than 150 children hundred children attending a local camp were also evacuated.

The facility is a residential care home for young people with complex psychological problems, behavioural problems or autism. Security staff said all residents were accounted for. 186 children attending a nearby summer camp were also evacuated.

The building is considered to be a total loss. It dates from 1981 and is suspected to contain asbestos. The authorities have cordoned off the area and asked residents to close their windows as a precautionary measure.

item.title: Weather warnings issued as temperatures set to hit 35C
item.description:
Weather warnings issued as temperatures set to hit 35C

July 29, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The national heat plan has been activated for the second time this summer as temperatures are set to reach between 30C and 35C in most parts of the Netherlands.

The meteorological office KNMI has issued code yellow warnings for the inland provinces of Overijssel, Gelderland, Noord-Brabant and Limburg, for Wednesday, and Thursday and Friday.

Temperatures are due to peak at 35C on Wednesday before falling slightly to around 32C on Thursday. On Saturday there will be a brief respite, with maximum temperatures of 25C, but new highs of 33C are forecast for Monday.

A lack of wind will make the heat feel more intense and temperatures will remain high at night, close to 20C in most parts of the country. Conditions will be cooler on the Wadden Islands, with a maximum temperature of 24C.

The national heat plan is invoked if there is a serious risk of temperatures above 27C for four days or longer.

It includes advice to pay extra attention to vulnerable people, drink more water to stay cool and be aware that medicines may work differently in warm conditions.

Last month the KNMI issued a red alert for heat for the first time. Schools and universities were closed, work was suspended on building sites and some supermarkets cancelled home deliveries.

item.title: Dutch tourist dies after boat overturns at waterfalls in Brazil
item.description:
Dutch tourist dies after boat overturns at waterfalls in Brazil

July 29, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A Dutch tourist has died and another is recovering in hospital after a boat overturned during a safari in Brazil.

The accident at the Iguaçu Falls, in the Iguaçu national park on the border with Argentina, happened on Tuesday afternoon and is being investigated by the Brazilian navy.

Local media said six Dutch nationals were on board the boat, including a family of four with two daughters, as well as two crew members. The man who died was reportedly the boyfriend of one of the daughters.

Investigations will focus on what caused the boat to overturn during the tour of the falls, which mark the boundary between the upper and lower Iguazu river.

Four of the victims, three women and a man, were given treatment at the scene by park staff but did not need to go to hospital. The victim died at Padre Germano Lauck Municipal Hospital in Foz do Iguaçu, where another member of the party is receiving treatment after being rescued by park workers.

The fire department confirmed the cause of death was drowning.

News website G1 reported that the falls were carrying 4.3 million litres of water per second at the time of the accident, nearly three times the normal level.

Tour operator Macuco Safari said in a statement that it regretted the incident and was providing assistance to the victims.

item.title: Thousands remember victims of Berlin Pride attack in Amsterdam
item.description:
Thousands remember victims of Berlin Pride attack in Amsterdam

July 29, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Thousands turned out in Amsterdam on Tuesday evening to lay flowers and commemorate the victims of an attack on Pride in Berlin.

At the weekend, a man drove a car into the crowd gathered in the German capital for the closing of Pride. One woman was killed and 29 others were injured.

The commemoration began with a moment of silence at the Homomonument, the national memorial to the victims of persecution for their sexual orientation, and attendees laid flowers at the memorial.

Amsterdam mayor Femke Halsema addressed the crowd, calling for courage and resilience. “We will win if we keep spreading hope loud and clear,” she said.

Many people are in the Dutch capital for Pride, which began on Saturday and has been combined with WorldPride for the first time. The famous canal parade will take place on August 1.

In other cities, groups also gathered to pay their respects. In Arnhem, a minute of silence was observed and the flag above city hall was flown at half-mast.

On Wednesday evening, there will be a gathering at Domplein in Utrecht.

On Sunday, German authorities killed the man suspected of carrying out the attack. He has been named as 21-year-old Abdul B. and was known to the police. He had already been convinced of violent threats and had previously travelled to Syria in an effort to join the Islamic State.

item.title: Philips reclaims €186m after Supreme Court rules tariffs illegal
item.description:
Philips reclaims €186m after Supreme Court rules tariffs illegal

July 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Health technology firm Philips has received an €186 million windfall after the United States Supreme Court ordered Donald Trump’s administration to refund illegally imposed tariffs.

The figures were included in the Amsterdam-based company’s latest quarterly report, which was published this week.

Trump imposed import tariffs on products from dozens of countries, as well as the European Union, in April last year.

But in February the Supreme Court upheld a judgment by a lower court that the president had wrongly used emergency powers to introduce the tariffs.

The US government was also ordered to refund and compensate companies that had paid the tariffs or whose business had been damaged as a result.

CEO Roy Jakobs said: “We started a legal case as soon as we could, which is why we are one of the first to get our money back.” Most of the repayments have already been made.

The extra income helped Philips increase its turnover by 4% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026. It recorded a profit of €386 million, but declining orders in both China and the US meant its share price dived by 10% on Tuesday.

Philips was founded in 1891 as a lightbulb manufacturer in Eindhoven and grew into one of the world’s largest producers of consumer electronics in the 20th century. Since 2010 it has focused on producing healthcare equipment.

item.title: Man arrested after disabled man found strangled in German hotel
item.description:
Man arrested after disabled man found strangled in German hotel

July 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A man has been arrested in Almelo in connection with the death of a Dutch tourist who was found strangled in a hotel room in Germany, close to the border.

The 35-year-old victim was discovered by staff on Sunday at Hotel Rheinpark in Rees, a German town about 30km south of Doetinchem.

A postmortem examination confirmed that the man had been strangled. He checked in to the hotel with another man on Saturday evening, but only the victim’s details were recorded in the guest register.

RTV Oost reported that the victim, from Enschede, was disabled and used a wheelchair. He was found dead by hotel staff on Sunday morning an hour after he was supposed to have checked out of the room.

German media said the pair arrived on Saturday in a Dutch-registered car from the Enschede area. They are understood to have gone to see a firework show in the area earlier in the day.

The 42-year-old man was arrested at his home in De Burcht, near Almelo, while he was walking towards his car, local media reported. He is suspected of being involved in the violent death of his companion. The vehicle also been impounded.

item.title: Drought and low river levels threaten Rhine cruises
item.description:
Drought and low river levels threaten Rhine cruises

July 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Low water levels are putting river cruises on the Rhine in jeopardy, with excursions being cancelled or cut short because boats are unable to access sections of the river.

Cruise operators told NOS they are anxiously monitoring the water level on a daily basis to see whether their scheduled trips can go ahead.

Teun Sijbrands, of SijFa Cruises, said 140 passengers boarded the Otello this week for a trip to Strasbourg, but it was unlikely that the boat would be able to travel that far.

The Otello has a depth of 1.45m, which is currently too deep to go further than Koblenz. “To get to Strasbourg we need more rain, but there’s no sign of it coming. That’s a big problem for us.

“If people don’t get the trip that’s described in the brochure, they can claim their money back.”

A spokesman for De Zonnebloem, an Arnhem-based ship that hosts cruises for people with disabilities, said: “We can’t go to Germany for the time being. Our first trip that way is planned for September, but it’s uncertain whether it will go ahead.”

Summer droughts are expected to become more likely as a result of climate change, making it increasingly difficult for river traffic.

At Lobith in Gelderland, the point at which the Rhine enters the Netherlands, the flow of water was down to 745 m3 per second in mid-July, less than half the average for the time of year of 1,900 m3.

Highways and waterways agency Rijkswaterstaat, which is responsible for river traffic, said the river level is unusually low for so early in the year, causing problems for both leisure cruises and cargo barges.

The problems are caused by low rainfall not just in the Netherlands, but further upstream in the Alps, rivers specialist Daniël van Putten told NOS. “That water just isn’t reaching us,” he said.

item.title: Body parts found on Texel identified as Afghan refugees
item.description:
Body parts found on Texel identified as Afghan refugees

July 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The police have identified the remains that washed on up a Texel beach in 2023 as two men from Afghanistan who are thought to have been trying to cross the North Sea to the United Kingdom.

A beachcomber made the gruesome discovery of legs and feet in October 2023.

Police could find no match to the DNA in missing persons databases, but aid organisations later notified Dutch authorities that two men from Afghanistan were missing. The Red Cross was able to collect samples from relatives and the police have now confirmed there was a match.

“With this DNA, it could be established that the body parts originated from two men aged 20 and 27 (in 2023), born in Afghanistan,” the police said in a statement.

No cause of death could be determined. The remains were buried in a city cemetery in Den Burg.

In 2014, the remains of a Syrian man, who was also thought to be trying to cross the Channel, washed up on Texel.
